name: Demo story — "Amara"
considering: Football academy trial vs. finishing her degree
chose: Continued university part-time while training with a semi-pro club
why: A trial gave honest feedback that she was not yet at the level clubs were signing, but coaches said two more serious years could change that.
whatHappened: Did not go fully professional, but the training discipline and club connections led to a sports management role after graduating.
biggestMistake: Waited too long to ask coaches for direct, honest feedback about her level.
biggestSuccess: Kept both paths alive long enough to gather real evidence before choosing.
wouldChooseAgain: Yes, with earlier and more honest feedback-seeking.
adviceToYoungerSelf: Ask the uncomfortable question sooner: 'Realistically, what level am I at?'

name: Demo story — "Marco"
wanted: To drop out and build a startup
considering: Leaving university entirely vs. building alongside it
chose: Built a small e-commerce project while continuing university
why: Family expected him to finish his degree, and he wasn't certain the business idea would work.
whatHappened: The first business idea failed within eight months, but the degree gave him a fallback and the experience shaped a second, more successful venture after graduating.
biggestMistake: Underestimated how much time both paths would actually take simultaneously.
biggestSuccess: Treated the first business as a real experiment rather than a one-shot bet.
adviceToYoungerSelf: Set a clear evidence checkpoint instead of an open-ended commitment.

name: Demo story — "Priya"
situation: Finishing secondary school, expected to pursue medicine
wanted: To study finance and economics instead
chose: Finance, after an honest conversation with her parents
why: She had strong grades in both but consistently sought out finance content on her own time, which she treated as the more reliable signal than grades alone.
whatHappened: Studied finance, and the family relationship was strained for about a year before her parents saw her genuine engagement with the field.
biggestMistake: Avoided the conversation with her parents for almost two years, which made the eventual disagreement harder than it needed to be.
biggestSuccess: Chose based on where her curiosity actually went, not just where she performed well.
adviceToYoungerSelf: Have the hard conversation early, not after the decision is already made.

name: Demo story — "Tomás"
situation: Studying computer science, playing amateur cricket-adjacent sport (futsal) competitively
wanted: To pursue software engineering, but felt guilty about giving up serious sport
considering: Full focus on tech career vs. one more season of competitive sport
chose: Took the one more season, on a fixed timeline, then moved fully into software engineering
why: He wanted to test the sport seriously rather than always wondering 'what if,' but was not willing to delay his career indefinitely.
whatHappened: The season confirmed sport would stay a serious hobby, not a career, which he says gave him closure rather than regret.
biggestMistake: None major — the fixed-timeline experiment worked as intended.
biggestSuccess: Defined in advance what 'enough evidence' would look like, so the decision didn't drag on indefinitely.
adviceToYoungerSelf: Trust a time-boxed experiment more than an open-ended feeling.
